Forest.position: dense woody vegetation cover dominated by tree canopy
family_visual_attributes: vegetation-dominated surfaces with green to dark green tones
limited presence of roofs, paved surfaces, or other built structures
soft, irregular natural boundaries rather than rigid geometric parcel edges
texture created by plant cover rather than bare soil or water smoothness
spatial patterns that follow terrain or natural drainage more than street grids
distinguishing_visual_attributes: dark green, relatively continuous canopy cover with coarse, mottled texture from tree crowns
few visible internal field divisions or plow/harvest striping compared with crop land
less uniform and less smooth texture than Herbaceous Vegetation Land or Pasture Land
absence of regular row patterns typical of Permanent Crop Land orchards or plantations
larger contiguous wooded patches with shadowed crown structure rather than small agricultural parcels

Annual Crop Land.position: temporarily cultivated arable fields used for seasonal crops within agricultural land
family_visual_attributes: land divided into distinct field or parcel units with visible boundaries
strong human-imposed geometric regularity such as rectangular or polygonal plots
mosaic pattern of adjacent plots with differing tones or textures
presence of access tracks, farm roads, or drainage/irrigation lines aligned with field edges
vegetation cover appears managed and spatially organized rather than naturally continuous
distinguishing_visual_attributes: plots often show bare soil or mixed soil-vegetation tones due to plowing, sowing, or harvest stages
fields commonly have uniform fine texture within each parcel but strong variation between neighboring parcels
lack of the repeated dot/grid pattern of tree crowns typical of Permanent Crop Land
more regular, sharply bounded cultivated parcels than the broader, less structured grassy expanses of Pasture Land or Herbaceous Vegetation Land
vegetation canopy is generally low and does not form the dense, continuous dark canopy seen in Forest

Highway or Road.position: linear transportation infrastructure within built-up land
family_visual_attributes: strong human-made geometry with straight lines, sharp edges, and regular boundaries
surfaces often appear gray, white, or dark and relatively non-vegetated compared with surrounding land
features are spatially organized in planned patterns such as blocks, corridors, or clusters
high contrast between constructed surfaces and adjacent vegetation or bare ground
presence of angular intersections, parallel edges, and other engineered layouts
distinguishing_visual_attributes: appears as elongated narrow corridors rather than compact building footprints or broad land parcels
shows continuous linear connectivity across the scene, often linking intersections and branching junctions
width is fairly uniform over long distances, unlike rivers which vary in width and have meandering edges
surface texture is smooth and homogeneous with little internal texture compared with building clusters
often bordered by roadside strips or aligned development, but the road itself remains a thin linear feature rather than an area-filling patch

Herbaceous Vegetation Land.position: non-woody vegetation cover dominated by grasses or low herbaceous plants, typically forming open continuous cover rather than tree canopy or cultivated field patterns
family_visual_attributes: vegetation-dominated surfaces with green to yellow-brown tones depending on season
soft, continuous textures rather than roofs, paved surfaces, or open water smoothness
little to no dense built structure or rectilinear urban block pattern
broad areal patches of land cover rather than narrow linear corridors
surface appearance often irregular or naturalistic in shape compared with engineered land parcels
distinguishing_visual_attributes: fine, fairly uniform grassy texture without the dark, coarse, shadowed canopy texture typical of Forest
absence of clear plow lines, row structure, or strongly segmented field blocks seen in Annual Crop Land
lack of orchard or vineyard striping, evenly spaced planting points, or repeated row geometry seen in Permanent Crop Land
more natural, unmanaged-looking patch boundaries and less enclosure or paddock subdivision than Pasture Land
typically open cover with few scattered trees and no dominant woody crown pattern

Pasture Land.position: grass-dominated grazing land within agricultural land
family_visual_attributes: Large contiguous land parcels with visible field or parcel boundaries
Vegetation cover dominates, with green to yellow-brown tones depending on growth stage
Human-managed spatial organization, often adjacent to roads, farm tracks, or other fields
Generally open landscapes with sparse built structures compared with urban classes
Patch-scale texture is more uniform and intentional than natural water bodies or dense urban areas
distinguishing_visual_attributes: Fields show relatively uniform grassy cover with fine, soft texture rather than strong row patterns or plowed striping
Parcel shapes are often irregular to moderately regular and appear as open grazing enclosures rather than tightly cultivated plots
Lacks the repeated linear planting geometry typical of Permanent Crop Land and the seasonal bare-soil contrast common in Annual Crop Land
Usually more homogeneous and managed-looking than Herbaceous Vegetation Land, with clearer field boundaries and less natural patchiness
Tree cover is sparse or absent across most of the parcel, unlike Forest

Permanent Crop Land.position: woody perennial cropland arranged in orchards, groves, vineyards, or other regularly planted permanent crop fields
family_visual_attributes: Large contiguous parcels with clear field or plot boundaries
Human-managed geometric patterns such as rectangular, elongated, or terraced plots
Vegetation cover showing more regularity and uniformity within parcels than natural vegetation
Presence of internal farm access tracks or straight edge alignments
Spectral and texture variation organized by parcel rather than irregular natural patchiness
distinguishing_visual_attributes: Regularly spaced planting pattern visible as dots, rows, or grid-like tree/vine alignments within fields
Repeating row texture that is more discrete and structured than the smoother cover of pasture or herbaceous land
Woody crop canopy appears in organized lines or clusters, unlike the dense continuous canopy of Forest
Field parcels often contain permanent row orientation that persists across the whole plot, unlike Annual Crop Land which is more often uniform continuous cover without visible tree spacing
Inter-row bare soil or grass strips may be visible between planted lines, creating alternating banded texture

Residential Buildings.position: low- to medium-density built structures arranged as housing neighborhoods within the urban built-up category
family_visual_attributes: dominance of man-made geometric forms such as rectangles, straight edges, and right angles
high proportion of impervious surfaces with gray, white, or dark roofs and paved areas
dense network of linear access features such as streets and driveways
parcelized, regular spatial organization rather than irregular natural textures
sharp boundaries and block-like patterns contrasting with surrounding vegetation or water
distinguishing_visual_attributes: many small to medium roof footprints clustered closely together rather than a few very large building blocks
buildings arranged along local street grids or cul-de-sacs, forming neighborhood blocks
noticeable mix of roofs, small yards, and scattered trees creating a finer-grained texture than industrial zones
less extensive open paved lots than Industrial Buildings, with roads serving houses rather than dominating the patch
pattern lacks the long parallel crop rows or uniform field parcels seen in Annual Crop Land and Permanent Crop Land

Industrial Buildings.position: large-scale industrial or warehouse building complexes within built-up areas
family_visual_attributes: dominance of man-made surfaces with rectilinear geometry
sharp, regular edges and block-like structures
extensive impervious cover in gray, white, or dark tones
organized layouts connected by road networks
sparse, fragmented vegetation compared with natural or agricultural classes
distinguishing_visual_attributes: very large rectangular roof footprints, often in clusters of warehouses or factory halls
broad paved yards, loading areas, or open storage surfaces surrounding buildings
buildings spaced farther apart and on larger parcels than the dense small-unit pattern of Residential Buildings
adjacency to wide access roads and parking lots, but with dominant building masses rather than only linear transport corridors
absence of the repetitive field rows, crop textures, or orchard grid patterns seen in Annual Crop Land and Permanent Crop Land

River.position: flowing inland watercourse within the water bodies category
family_visual_attributes: surfaces appear smooth or fine-textured compared with vegetated or built-up areas
typically darker blue, dark green, or gray tones depending on depth, sediment, and illumination
boundaries are often sharply contrasted against adjacent land cover
lack internal roof patterns, crop rows, or dense canopy texture
often form continuous connected shapes rather than many small discrete objects
distinguishing_visual_attributes: long, narrow, elongated shape that traverses the scene rather than forming a broad enclosed basin
sinuous or branching channel pattern with visible bends and tributary-like connections
width usually varies gradually along its course instead of staying uniformly engineered
banks are irregular natural edges rather than straight paved margins or lane-marked surfaces
commonly bordered by thin strips of riparian vegetation or floodplain land following the channel

Sea or Lake.position: large open inland or coastal water surface within the water bodies category
family_visual_attributes: smooth or nearly textureless surface compared with vegetated or built-up areas
generally uniform dark blue, blue-green, or gray tone across broad areas
lack of field boundaries, building footprints, or road grid patterns within the water surface
edges defined by shorelines or banks that sharply separate water from land
specular brightness or sun-glint patches may appear on parts of the surface
distinguishing_visual_attributes: broad contiguous water expanse occupying a large area rather than a narrow elongated channel
compact, rounded, lobed, or irregular basin/coastal shape instead of a thin meandering linear form
interior is largely uninterrupted by bars, banks, or frequent crossings that segment the feature
shoreline encloses or borders a wide open-water area with much greater width-to-length ratio than a river
